name: Negotiate documents and close private transactions
summary: After an investment is approved, in-house legal counsel and external law firms negotiate the purchase, shareholder, credit or fund documents, keep the final terms within the approval, and get them signed by authorised officers of the fund's holding subsidiaries. Deals that cannot close at signing wait for merger control and foreign investment clearances and third-party consents. At closing, the deal team and Tax check the funds flow, operations wires the money and the documents go to the asset management teams. Counterparty turnaround and regulatory waiting periods set the pace, multi-jurisdiction signatures are slow to collect, and about one approved deal in five never closes.

baseline.org_archetype: A very large Canadian national pension fund manager closing direct private equity, real asset, credit and fund transactions worldwide through investment holding subsidiaries.
baseline.notes: Starts at committee or Board approval; much negotiation of the purchase agreement starts earlier in diligence and continues here. Payment release is done in the operations cash settlement process.

trigger: The Portfolio Execution Committee or the Board approves a transaction and Legal receives the approval decision.
end_state: The transaction is closed, funds are settled and documents are handed over, or the deal is lost or terminated.

volume.seasonality: Peaks before calendar year end and fiscal year end (March 31).

evidence.note: Process map estimate of about 30 closings started a month across PE, RA, CI and fund commitments; at the modelled loss rate about 23 close, near the 20 closings a month demand driver.

steps.name: Assign counsel and open the closing matter
steps.description: A legal director reads the approval decision and conditions, assigns in-house counsel and a paralegal based on workload and jurisdiction, and confirms the external law firm already working on the deal.

evidence.note: In-house legal supports complex deal structures with external counsel. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Build the closing checklist and signing plan
steps.description: The paralegal opens the matter file and builds the closing checklist: documents, signatories, subsidiary resolutions, regulatory filings, third-party consents and closing deliverables, with owners and dates.

evidence.note: Common legal practice for multi-party closings. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Instruct external counsel on the approved terms
steps.description: Legal counsel sends external counsel the approved price limits, conditions and structure, agrees a fee estimate and the drafting plan for the definitive agreements.

control.basis: Expense management policy with seniority-based approval of external legal fees

evidence.note: External counsel advise on transactions; legal fees are transaction-related expenses. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Negotiate definitive agreement drafts
steps.description: Legal counsel and external counsel turn the purchase or credit agreement, shareholder or partnership agreement and disclosure schedules, keep an issues list and hold negotiation calls with the counterparty's counsel.

error.defect_description: A negotiated change is not carried into all related documents.

evidence.note: Draft agreement circulated and negotiated to a definitive agreement. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Wait for the counterparty's response
steps.description: The seller, sponsor, borrower or general partner and their counsel review the draft and return a markup. In auctions the seller may instead choose another bidder.

next.condition: seller picks another bidder or walks away

evidence.note: Turnaround and loss share are the author's estimates; a share of approved final bids lose the auction.

steps.name: Resolve open business points (PE)
steps.description: The PE deal principal reviews the counterparty's markup with legal counsel, decides price adjustment, indemnity, governance and covenant points within the approval, and gives instructions for the next turn.

evidence.note: Negotiation rounds on the draft agreement; about 45% of closings. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Resolve open business points (Real Assets)
steps.description: The Real Assets deal principal reviews the counterparty's markup with legal counsel, decides price adjustment, indemnity, governance and covenant points within the approval, and gives instructions for the next turn.

evidence.note: Negotiation rounds on the draft agreement; about 35% of closings. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Resolve open business points (credit)
steps.description: The credit deal principal reviews the counterparty's markup with legal counsel, decides price adjustment, indemnity, governance and covenant points within the approval, and gives instructions for the next turn.

evidence.note: Negotiation rounds on the draft agreement; about 20% of closings. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Confirm tax structure and tax terms
steps.description: A tax senior associate checks the final structure steps, holding entities, tax representations, indemnities and withholding provisions against the tax structure memo and signs off or asks for changes.

control.basis: Tax department sign-off on transaction structure and tax terms

evidence.note: Tax advisory work is part of private transactions. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Confirm final terms are within the approval
steps.description: The legal director compares the final price, leverage, governance terms and conditions with the committee's approval and conditions, and records that they fit or that a new approval is needed.

control.basis: Investment Management Authorities: execution must stay within approved terms

next.condition: counterparty will not meet approved terms, team walks away

evidence.note: Investment Management Authorities bound what can be signed. Shares are estimates.

steps.name: Approve changed terms by circulation
steps.description: The committee chair reviews a short note on the changed price or terms and approves by email, or asks for the item to return to a full meeting.

control.basis: Investment Management Authorities: re-approval for material changes

evidence.note: Re-approval under the approval authorities; process is the author's assumption.

steps.name: Obtain subsidiary resolutions and signing authorities
steps.description: Legal counsel prepares resolutions for the investment holding subsidiaries, collects approvals from their directors, some of them in Luxembourg or other jurisdictions, and confirms authorised signatories and incumbency certificates.

control.basis: Signing authority policy and corporate governance of investment holding subsidiaries

evidence.note: Private investments are held through investment holding subsidiaries. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Update the restricted list for signing
steps.description: A compliance officer adds the target or issuer to the restricted list before signing or announcement and confirms the deal team and Legal remain behind the information barrier.

control.basis: Securities law insider trading prohibitions and the Code of Conduct restricted list

evidence.note: Pre-clearance and restrictions on personal trading in prescribed circumstances; the restricted list mechanism is the author's description. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Collect signatures and exchange signature pages
steps.description: The paralegal circulates execution versions, collects e-signatures or scanned pages from authorised signatories in several offices, and exchanges pages with the counterparty's counsel at signing.

evidence.note: Private deals often sign and close together; deferred closings wait for regulatory approvals. Shares are estimates.

steps.name: Prepare and file merger and foreign investment notices
steps.description: Legal counsel works with local counsel to prepare competition filings (for example HSR or EU) and foreign investment filings (for example CFIUS or UK national security), supplies the fund's ownership and government relationship information and answers regulators' questions.

control.basis: Merger control and foreign investment laws (HSR Act, CFIUS rules, UK National Security and Investment Act and others): no closing before clearance

evidence.note: HSR 30-day waiting period; CFIUS mandatory declarations for some foreign government investors; UK mandatory notification in 17 sectors.

steps.name: Wait for regulatory clearances and third-party consents
steps.description: Regulators run their waiting periods and reviews, and landlords, lenders, partners or customers give change of control consents. A few deals are blocked or pass the outside date.

next.condition: regulator blocks or outside date passes

evidence.note: HSR 30 days, CFIUS 45 plus 45 days, UK 30 working days plus 30 and 45; closing takes a few weeks to over a year. The range is the author's reading.

steps.name: Track conditions precedent and chase deliverables
steps.description: The paralegal runs weekly checklist calls, records each condition and deliverable as satisfied and chases counterparties, local counsel and the insurance broker for outstanding items.

evidence.note: Includes binding of warranty insurance where used. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Prepare closing deliverables and bring-down certificates
steps.description: Legal counsel settles officer and bring-down certificates, legal opinions, payoff letters and the closing statement with external counsel, and asks counsel for the funds flow memo.

evidence.note: Closing follows satisfaction of all conditions. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Check the funds flow memo (PE)
steps.description: The PE deal principal checks the funds flow memo prepared by counsel against the purchase agreement and the final closing statement: price, adjustments, debt payoffs, fees and each payee.

error.defect_description: Wrong adjustment or payee amount carried into the wire request.

evidence.note: Funds flow review is standard closing practice; wire fraud risk makes payee checks important. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Check the funds flow memo (Real Assets)
steps.description: The Real Assets deal principal checks the funds flow memo prepared by counsel against the purchase agreement and the final closing statement: price, adjustments, debt payoffs, fees and each payee.

error.defect_description: Wrong adjustment or payee amount carried into the wire request.

evidence.note: Funds flow review is standard closing practice; wire fraud risk makes payee checks important. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Check the funds flow memo (credit)
steps.description: The credit deal principal checks the funds flow memo prepared by counsel against the purchase agreement and the final closing statement: price, adjustments, debt payoffs, fees and each payee.

error.defect_description: Wrong adjustment or payee amount carried into the wire request.

evidence.note: Funds flow review is standard closing practice; wire fraud risk makes payee checks important. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Review withholding and tax payments in the funds flow
steps.description: The tax senior associate checks withholding, transfer taxes and any tax clearance certificates required for payments to non-resident sellers and confirms the amounts in the funds flow.

control.basis: Income tax withholding and transfer tax rules in each jurisdiction

evidence.note: Withholding and transfer tax rules apply to cross-border payments; general knowledge. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Send the closing funds request to operations
steps.description: Legal counsel sends direct operations the signed funds flow, payee wire details obtained from counsel and the closing date, so operations can set up the investment and verify and release the wires.

control.basis: Legal requests the funds; operations verifies wire instructions by call-back and releases with two authorised approvals

evidence.note: Operations support closings with system setups and settlements; payment details must be verified through a second channel. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Hold the closing call and release signatures
steps.description: On the closing day legal counsel confirms with counterparty counsel that all deliverables are in escrow and the wires have arrived, then releases signature pages and declares the deal closed.

evidence.note: Standard closing practice. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Send regulatory and ownership filing requests
steps.description: Legal counsel lists the post-closing filings triggered by the deal, such as ownership reports, foreign investment notifications and beneficial ownership updates, and sends requests to Compliance.

control.basis: Post-closing ownership and foreign investment filing rules in each market

evidence.note: Securities and foreign direct investment requirements are monitored. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Compile closing set and hand over the deal
steps.description: The paralegal collects final executed documents from external counsel, files the closing set, updates the pipeline system and sends key terms and obligations to asset management, fund monitoring and operations.

evidence.note: Closing sets often take weeks to arrive from external counsel. Times are the author's estimates.

exceptions.name: Lost after approval
exceptions.description: The seller picks another bidder or the counterparty walks away during final negotiation.

exceptions.name: Terms move outside the approval
exceptions.description: Price, leverage or governance terms change; the chair approves by circulation or the deal stops.

exceptions.name: Structure change late in negotiation
exceptions.description: Tax or counterparty changes the structure, and documents are redrafted.

exceptions.name: Regulatory review or consents
exceptions.description: Closing waits for merger control, foreign investment clearances and third-party consents; a second request or national security investigation can add months.

exceptions.name: Funds flow correction
exceptions.description: Tax or the deal team finds a wrong amount or payee and counsel reissues the funds flow.

exceptions.name: Deal blocked or outside date passes
exceptions.description: A regulator blocks the deal or conditions are not met by the outside date.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from approval to closing or termination
benchmarks.population: Private transactions by large institutional investors

evidence.note: Negotiation 6-8 weeks; closing a few weeks after signing for private companies to over a year with regulatory hurdles; HSR waiting period 30 days. The p50 and p90 are the author's reading for a mix with about 38% sign-and-close deals.
30 days unless early termination; extended by a Second Request.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days review, plus 45 days investigation as needed

evidence.note: Assessment after call-in 30 working days extendable by 45.

benchmarks.population: BEC incidents reported to IC3 and partners

evidence.note: 241,206 incidents.

pain_points.description: Each round of drafting waits days for the counterparty, and business points go back and forth between counsel and the deal team.

evidence.note: Negotiation stage of 6-8 weeks.

pain_points.description: Regulatory waiting periods and national security reviews set the closing date and can add months; filings need the fund's government ownership details in each country.

evidence.note: Statutory review periods.

pain_points.description: Collecting resolutions and signatures from holding subsidiaries and signatories in several offices and time zones delays signing.

evidence.note: Holding subsidiary structure; delay is the author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Funds flow memos are assembled late and checked by hand; payee errors and wire fraud attempts are a known risk at closing.

evidence.note: US$43 billion of exposed BEC losses 2016 to 2021.

sources.supports: External Funds Operations team of nine assists investment closings through documentation review, system setups, transaction entries and settlements

assumptions: The process starts at approval; purchase agreement markups started during diligence continue here.

About 16% of approved deals are lost to another bidder or a counterparty walk-away (a 10% chance at each drafting round), 4% stop because terms move outside the approval, and about 1% fail on regulation, so about 78% close. This matches roughly 30 cases a month starting and 20 to 23 closing.
38% of signings close at the same time (fund subscriptions, many credit deals and small private deals); 62% wait for regulatory clearances or consents.

Department shares (PE 45%, RA 35%, CI 20%) are estimates; the funds flow check branch is drawn independently of the earlier negotiation branch, which does not change costs because the three principal roles have the same loaded cost.
External law firm hours are not modelled as roles; they appear only as waits and as work in the in-house counsel steps.
The Competition Bureau page could not be opened, so Canadian merger review times are not cited; US and UK rules are cited instead because many of the fund's deals are foreign.

legal_md is listed for this process in the organisation file but is not given a step; directors assign and check matters and the MD's time is mainly escalation. tfm_cio is added for re-approval by circulation.
